    Convert sm_corpus to bibliometrix format

    Source: R/interop-bibliometrix.R
    sm_to_bibliometrix.Rd

    Converts an sm_corpus to the data frame format used by bibliometrix::biblioAnalysis() and the other functions of bibliometrix: one row per work and one column per Web of Science field tag. This enables using bibliometrix's analysis functions on corpora built with scimapR.

    Usage

    sm_to_bibliometrix(
  corpus,
  keep_extra = TRUE,
  db = c("auto", "ISI", "scimapR"),
  ...
)

    Arguments

    corpus

    An sm_corpus object.

    keep_extra

    Logical. If TRUE (default), the columns without a field tag follow the tag columns, as in earlier versions: the other works columns (such as work_id and source_id), country_code and SO_ISSN. FALSE returns the tag columns only.

    db

    Value of the DB column. "auto" (default) writes "ISI" when every work comes from Web of Science and "scimapR" otherwise; "ISI" and "scimapR" write that value. See Details.

    ...

    Additional arguments (currently unused).

    Value

    A data frame with class c("bibliometrixDB", "data.frame"), one row per work in the order of corpus$works, with SR as row names. Every tag column is present, NA where the corpus holds no data.

    Details

    Field tags

    • AU: authors as SURNAME INITIALS, AF: full names as SURNAME, GIVEN NAMES; one entry per author of the work, in position order and separated by ;, from authors$display_name through authorships. An author with several address rows appears once; authors without a name are left out.

    • TI, AB: works$title, works$abstract; TI_raw and AB_raw hold them in their stored case, as bibliometrix::convert2df() does.

    • SO, J9, JI: sources$display_name, and the optional columns sources$abbreviation and sources$iso_abbreviation.

    • SN, EI: sources$issn_l (else the first value of sources$issn) and the next distinct value of sources$issn.

    • C1: one segment per distinct address of the work, [AUTHOR A; AUTHOR B] ADDRESS, with the authors (AF form) in position order, joined by ; ; from authorships$raw_affiliation.

    • RP: one segment per corresponding author (authorships$is_corresponding), SURNAME, INITIALS (CORRESPONDING AUTHOR), ADDRESS with the author's first address, joined by ; .

    • EM: the e-mail addresses of the optional column authorships$email.

    • CR: references$cited_raw in ref_index order, separated by ;; NR: the number of items in CR.

    • DE: author keywords, see below; DE_raw holds them in their stored case. ID: the concepts of the indexer_keyword family of sm_concept_vocabularies() (such as Keywords Plus or MeSH). WC: the vocabulary wos-category (Web of Science categories); SC: the vocabulary wos-subject-category (research areas). Terms are joined by ; .

    • DT, LA, PY, TC, DI, PM: works$type, language, year, cited_by_count, doi and pmid.

    • UT: the Web of Science accession number, provenance$source_id_external of the work's first provenance row with source == "wos", else a work_id that starts with WOS:.

    • DB: see below. SR: the short reference FIRST AUTHOR, YEAR, J9 (with SO where J9 is missing), made unique by appending -a, -b, ... to repeats; SR_FULL keeps it without the suffixes.

    With keep_extra = TRUE, country_code holds the country codes of authorships$country_code, one per authorship row (author and address), and SO_ISSN holds sources$issn_l. The export has no AU_CO column, as data from bibliometrix::convert2df() has none: bibliometrix::metaTagExtraction(M, "AU_CO") adds the country names that bibliometrix reads from C1 and uses for its country analyses.

    Conventions

    Like bibliometrix::convert2df() for Web of Science files, the export upper-cases AU, AF, TI, SO, J9, JI, AB, C1, RP, EM, CR (including the DOIs in it), DE, ID, WC, SC, DT and LA. DI, UT, SN, EI and PM are written as stored, so DI keeps the lower-case DOIs of the scimapR readers. Upper-casing uses toupper(), whose result for non-ASCII letters depends on the locale.

    Names: a display_name with a comma is read as Surname, Given names. Otherwise an entry of authors$display_name_alternatives in that form that agrees with the name gives the surname, so a surname of several words such as "Garcia Lopez" stays whole; sm_read_wos() keeps the names of the file there. Else initials at the end of the name (single letters, or capitals with periods, as in "Chen W." from sm_read_scopus()) follow the surname, and otherwise the last word is the surname, together with the lower-case particles before it ("Anna van der Berg" gives VAN DER BERG A). Particles never become initials. Without such a spelling, a surname of several words without particles ("Maria Garcia Lopez") keeps only its last word, and a name such as "SMITH JA" is read as given names followed by the surname. The given names of AF are the longest spelling at hand, the initials of AU the shortest. Corpora read by sm_read_wos() store the AU form of a name (such as "J Smith"), so their AF holds initials.

    CR items are written in the Web of Science form SURNAME INITIALS, YEAR, SOURCE, ...: an item Surname, IN, YEAR, ... (with a comma after the surname, as some exports write it) becomes SURNAME IN, YEAR, .... Other items, such as titles or OpenAlex IDs, are only upper-cased. Because ; separates the items of AU, AF, C1, RP, CR, DE, ID, WC and SC, a ; inside an item becomes ,.

    DE holds the author keywords of each work: the concepts of the author_keyword family of sm_concept_vocabularies() (author-keywords, manual-tags). A work without author keywords gets its OpenAlex concepts (openalex) instead, so corpora built from OpenAlex keep their DE; other vocabularies (Keywords Plus, MeSH, categories, arXiv and bioRxiv subjects) never enter DE. A work with neither has DE = NA.

    DB: with db = "auto", a corpus whose works all come from Web of Science (each has a provenance row with source == "wos", or a work_id that starts with WOS:) gets "ISI", the value bibliometrix::convert2df() writes for Web of Science files, so that bibliometrix::histNetwork() and bibliometrix::rpys() accept it. Other corpora get "scimapR", because bibliometrix reads "ISI" data as Web of Science records; db = "ISI" declares a corpus whose CR items are in Web of Science form anyway.

    RP follows authorships$is_corresponding: it names the authors flagged TRUE and is NA for a work without one. sm_read_wos() takes the corresponding authors from the RP field of the file, sm_read_openalex_json() and sm_fetch_openalex() from the OpenAlex records, sm_read_dimensions() from the Corresponding Authors column, sm_fetch_biorxiv() from the bioRxiv API and as_sm_corpus() from RP. The other readers and fetchers record the corresponding author as unknown (NA), so their corpora export RP = NA. Corpora built from tables keep the flags of their tables.

    as_sm_corpus() reads the result back: the round trip keeps the works, their DOIs and years, the authors of each work, their addresses and the corresponding authors.

    References

    Aria, M. & Cuccurullo, C. (2017). bibliometrix: An R-tool for comprehensive science mapping analysis. Journal of Informetrics, 11(4), 959-975. doi:10.1016/j.joi.2017.08.007

    Examples

    corpus <- sm_example_corpus(n_works = 10, n_authors = 5,
                            with_embeddings = FALSE)
M <- sm_to_bibliometrix(corpus, keep_extra = FALSE)
class(M)
#> [1] "bibliometrixDB" "data.frame"    
M[1:3, c("AU", "PY", "SO", "DB")]
#>                                                                      AU   PY
#> ZHANG M, 2023, PLOS ONE   ZHANG M;PETROVA D;SMITH C;JOHNSON H;FISCHER R 2023
#> JOHNSON H, 2019, PNAS                         JOHNSON H;SMITH C;ZHANG M 2019
#> FISCHER R, 2018, PLOS ONE           FISCHER R;SMITH C;ZHANG M;JOHNSON H 2018
#>                                 SO      DB
#> ZHANG M, 2023, PLOS ONE   PLOS ONE scimapR
#> JOHNSON H, 2019, PNAS         PNAS scimapR
#> FISCHER R, 2018, PLOS ONE PLOS ONE scimapR

# a corpus from Web of Science records
fix <- readRDS(sm_example_files("example_realuse_corpus.rds"))
M <- sm_to_bibliometrix(fix)
unique(M$DB)
#> [1] "ISI"
M$C1[1]
#> [1] "[VAHRENKAMP, SVENJA] ZENT INST SANITATSWESENS NORDSTADT, DEPT OCCUPAT MED, D-99003 NORDSTADT, GERMANY.; [HOEKSTRA, PRIYA] LAKESIDE UNIV, DEPT EPIDEMIOL, LAKESIDE, MA 02999 USA.; [PIEPER, CLARA; NOLTING, MATTHIAS; LUTTERBECK, MARIE] ZENT INST SANITATSWESENS NORDSTADT, DEPT HYG, D-99003 NORDSTADT, GERMANY.; [ENGELKE, CLARA] FED ARMED FORCES INST MICROBIOL, DEPT VIROL, D-99002 SOUTHCITY, GERMANY.; [ENGELKE, CLARA] UNIV NORTHTOWN, DEPT MICROBIOL, NORTHTOWN, GERMANY.; [PETROVIC, HANNAH] SOUTHCITY MED SCH, DEPT INFECT DIS, D-99012 SOUTHCITY, GERMANY."
# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("bibliometrix", quietly = TRUE)) {
  results <- bibliometrix::biblioAnalysis(M, sep = ";")
}
# }
